verdict.reasoning: Patient reports shortness of breath over the last hour while sitting and watching TV: 'just like over the last hour, I've started to feel, like, a bit short of breath' and doctor confirms 'you've noticed shortness of breath for just an hour, while sitting and watching TV?'.

Onset is recent and at rest: 'just like over the last hour, I've started to feel, like, a bit short of breath' while 'watching TV' and when asked 'Have you noticed anything like this before?' patient replies 'Um, no.' indicating no prior episodes.
Patient states 'I , I started with a cough yesterday.' and confirms when doctor summarizes 'And, yesterday you noticed a cough?' Patient: 'Yeah.' No sputum is described, consistent with a dry cough.

Palpitations and chest soreness on deep inspiration are supported: 'my heart, it's really going' and 'when you take a very deep breath in?... my chest feels sore, but so does my C-section scar.' She denies chest pain generally: 'And, the shortness of breath, does it cause any pain in your chest? Patient: Um, no.' However, there is no mention of sputum or hemoptysis in the transcript, so 'denies sputum and hemoptysis' adds new information.
Timing and tenderness are documented: 'I had a C-section a few weeks ago.' 'Yeah, four weeks.' and 'my chest feels sore, but so does my C-section scar. You know, it's, it's all tender.'
Patient confirms C-section 4 weeks ago: 'I had a C-section a few weeks ago.' and when asked 'how long ago was that?' she replies 'Yeah, four weeks.'

Medication name and timing supported: 'they gave me some, uh, Codeine.' and 'I've been taking that fairly, fairly regularly. But, probably haven't taken it for a week.' which corresponds to last dose about one week ago.
Allergy and unspecified reaction supported: Patient: 'I'm allergic to Ibuprofen, though.' Doctor asks reaction, patient: 'I don't know. Sorry.' Thus allergy is present and reaction is unspecified.
Patient reports maternal history: 'my mum's had, uh, clots in her legs before.' which matches a history of leg clots in her mother.

Transcript confirms she is with baby ('Are you with baby at the moment? Patient: Yes, I am.') and the baby is fine, and that her partner exists and is at work ('My partner's at work.'). It does not state that she lives with the partner or explicitly that she is the primary caregiver of a 4‑week‑old infant (infant’s exact age as 4 weeks is inferred from C‑section timing but not explicitly tied to infant age), so this adds social details not stated.
Doctor asks 'Is anyone else with you at home?' Patient: 'Uh, no. My partner's at work.' indicating she was alone (aside from baby) at the time of the call.

Pulse count and tachycardia are documented: patient counts 'thirty' beats over 15 seconds and doctor responds 'your heart is running slightly fast at the moment,' which corresponds to ~120 bpm and tachycardia.

The fact says these features 'rule out pulmonary embolism,' but the doctor explicitly raises concern for clots/PE: 'what I'm worried about at the moment is, given that you've had a C-section... Some people can suffer with clots... in your lungs.' The clinical reasoning is the opposite (rule in concern, not rule out).
Post‑operative status 4 weeks after C‑section is established: 'I had a C-section a few weeks ago.' and 'Yeah, four weeks.' clearly indicating she is 4 weeks post‑op.

Transcript notes palpitations ('my heart, it's really going' and doctor: 'you're feeling your heart more than normal?') and suggests they may be due to 'the shortness of breath and some of the pain that you're under.' There is no attribution specifically to anxiety or pain related to a 'suspected pulmonary embolism'; PE is discussed as a possibility but not tied as the cause of palpitations, so this causal interpretation is added.

Emergency evaluation and transport options are discussed: 'It might be worth you going into the hospital to get checked out a bit further.' and 'there's two ways... I can call an ambulance. Or, you can take yourself to the hospital with baby.' Patient: 'I will, I will take myself.' Doctor: 'go fairly quickly and take some bits for baby at the same time.'
Doctor advises holding Codeine: 'if you're taking any medications like Codeine, don't, don't take them for the time being.'

Doctor educates on increased clot risk postpartum and treatment: 'given that you've had a C-section... Some people can suffer with clots... in your lungs.' and 'It's quite a common thing to happen... needs to be checked out in the hospital first.' and 'if that does become the case, they can give you something to reduce the clot.' This explains clot risk and need for hospital assessment/treatment (e.g., anticoagulation/imaging).

There is no discussion in the transcript about seeking help sooner if symptoms worsen en route or explicitly calling emergency services if deterioration occurs. This safety‑net advice is not mentioned.
